gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Amazfit Active Max's '25 days' and '64 h GPS' figures are lab claims: the5krunner measured continuous GPS at about 40 hours, and only with minimum brightness and the always-on display off.
standout_why: I read our page (dealectric.com, 2026-11-02 version) and tried to open the cited rivals: us.amazfit.com/products/bip-6 returned HTTP 429, and Tom's Guide (Bip 6 vs SE 3) came back cut off after the headline. Our page already gives the Active Max's heavy-use figure (13 days) and always-on figure (10 days), and ChatGPT already passed on 'Bip 6 rated for only six days of heavy use' from our page. So the 'typical vs heavy' split is not new. The part that is new is putting all the picks under one condition: the Bip Max heavy-use figure, what Amazfit counts as 'typical' use, and measured results. That part is not sourced from pages I opened, because Amazfit's US, UK and India stores all returned 429 and Wareable and Android Authority returned 403.
decides: This supports the Active Max as the pick, not the cheaper watches. Its heavy-use rating (13 days, per our page citing Amazfit) is the closest any candidate gets to two weeks. The Bip 6 (14 days typical) only reaches 14 days under Amazfit's light 'typical' profile. The5krunner's tests also show the Active Max's headline figures shrink in real use (about 40 h GPS against 64 h claimed). So a shopper who needs a real 14 days should treat the typical-use number as a best case. If the Bip Max heavy-use figure (10 days, snippet only) is confirmed on Amazfit's page, the footnote for the table becomes: under the same heavy-use profile, only the Active Max comes near 14 days.

unsourced: Amazfit's definition of 'typical' and 'heavy' use (search snippets say: static watch face, 24-h wear, heart rate every ~5 min for typical and every ~1 min for heavy). Amazfit's US, UK and India product pages all returned HTTP 429 on several tries, and the Bip 6 user manual PDF (support.amazfit.com) had no extractable text through the fetch tool.
Bip Max heavy-use battery (10 days per snippet), always-on battery (7 days per snippet) and GPS (40 h per snippet), plus 550 mAh: the Amazfit Bip Max page returned 429 every time.
Bip 6 heavy-use battery (6 days per snippet), battery saver (26 days per snippet) and 340 mAh: the Amazfit Bip 6 page returned 429 and the manual PDF text could not be extracted.

Measured Bip 6 drain from named reviewers (TechAdvisor about 10%/day with always-on off; Android Authority about 16% per 24 h with always-on, GPS and sleep tracking, per snippets): Android Authority and Wareable returned 403; the TechRadar and Tom's Guide pages came back cut off after the headline.

Measured Active Max multi-day battery (Wareable, 7–10 days with always-on display and daily GPS, per snippet): Wareable returned 403; the Tom's Guide and Live Science reviews came back cut off after the headline.
Garmin Forerunner 55 smartwatch-mode battery and its test conditions: the garmin.com/en-US/p/741137 page returned only navigation, with no specs.
Whether pairing with an iPhone rather than Android changes Amazfit battery life: I found no maker statement or reviewer test either way.
